source_evidence.observation: A_tilde is introduced as a BLR representation of a dense matrix A: there are p by p blocks of size b by b, n = pb, diagonal blocks remain dense, and off-diagonal blocks are low-rank approximations with the factor orientation in (2.3). Their minimum ranks satisfy the tolerance in (2.4), with beta_ij = ||A_ij|| for a local threshold or beta_ij = ||A|| for a global threshold. The page also declares every unsubscripted norm in the analysis to be the Frobenius norm. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 953, Section 2.1, eqs. (2.2)-(2.4)]

The arithmetic model is fl(x op y) = (x op y)(1 + delta), |delta| <= u, for op in {+, -, multiplication, division}. The paper defines gamma_k = ku/(1-ku) when ku < 1 and permits positive non-integer gamma indices. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 954, eq. (2.5) and following gamma definition]

A truncated-SVD compression is modeled as A_tilde_ij = A_ij + Delta_A_ij with ||Delta_A_ij|| <= epsilon beta_ij. Rounding errors in forming these approximations are ignored, and the analysis assumes that u is safely smaller than epsilon. [PDF p. 5, printed p. 955, Assumption 2.1]

The symbol r denotes the largest rank among off-diagonal blocks of the computed BLR LU factors. It can exceed the input BLR rank and is determined by the matrix and threshold rather than being independently tunable. [PDF p. 12, printed p. 962, opening of Section 4]

Algorithm 1 is the UFC order: update, factor, then compress. Its factorization theorem assumes that the un-tilded A is nonsingular and that the algorithm runs to completion. [PDF p. 13, printed p. 963, Algorithm 1 and Theorem 4.1]

For UFC, the simplified finite bounds use scaled local or global compression parameters: the resulting truncation contribution is epsilon||A|| or p epsilon||A||, respectively. The surrounding text says scaled thresholds are used thereafter to simplify the bounds. [PDF p. 17, printed p. 967, eqs. (4.13)-(4.15)]

Table 1 gives xi_p as 1 for local/no recompression, p for global/no recompression, p for local/with recompression, and p^2/sqrt(6) for global/with recompression. Theorem 4.2 gives the UFC factorization bound with c = b + 2r^(3/2) + p, conditional on nonsingularity and running to completion. [PDF p. 19, printed p. 969, Table 1 and Theorem 4.2, eq. (4.16)]

Algorithm 2 is the UCF order: update, compress, then factor. Theorem 4.3 assumes that A is nonsingular and Algorithm 2 runs to completion, and gives the corresponding BLR factorization bound with c = b + 2r^(3/2) + p and xi_p from Table 1. [PDF p. 21, printed p. 971, Algorithm 2 and Theorem 4.3, eq. (4.17)]

The block triangular solve processes block vectors using the previously computed blocks. It produces joint matrix and right-hand-side perturbations bounded by gamma_c_tri||T_tilde|| and gamma_p||v||, where c_tri = b + r^(3/2) + p. [PDF p. 23, printed p. 973, Theorem 4.4, eq. (4.21)]

Theorem 4.5 permits factors from either Algorithm 1 or Algorithm 2 and states (A + Delta_A)x_hat = v + Delta_v, with ||Delta_A|| <= (xi_p epsilon + gamma_p)||A|| + gamma_(3c)||L_tilde||||U_tilde|| + O(u epsilon) and ||Delta_v|| <= gamma_p(||v|| + ||L_tilde||||U_tilde||||x_hat||) + O(u^2), where c = b + 2r^(3/2) + p. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, Theorem 4.5, eqs. (4.23)-(4.25)]

Before normwise simplification, the proof composes the factorization and solve perturbations exactly: the final matrix perturbation is the factorization perturbation plus Delta_L_tilde U_tilde, L_tilde Delta_U_tilde, and Delta_L_tilde Delta_U_tilde; the final right-hand-side perturbation is the first-solve perturbation plus L_tilde Delta_y_hat and Delta_L_tilde Delta_y_hat. [PDF p. 25, printed p. 975, proof of Theorem 4.5]

binders: The block parameters are p and b, with a p by p block partition into b by b blocks and total dimension n = pb. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 953, Section 2.1 after eq. (2.3)]
The printed Theorem 4.5 binds A_tilde in R^(n x n), described as a pb by pb BLR matrix, and v in R^n. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, Theorem 4.5 opening sentence]
The surrounding BLR definition also associates A_tilde with an un-tilded dense matrix A in R^(n x n). [PDF p. 3, printed p. 953, Section 2.1, eqs. (2.2)-(2.4)]

L_tilde and U_tilde are computed BLR LU factors produced by either Algorithm 1 or Algorithm 2; y_hat and x_hat are the computed triangular-solve results. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, Theorem 4.5; PDF p. 25, printed p. 975, proof]

The quantifier order is: for the stated matrix, right-hand side, threshold configuration, and completed computation, there exist final perturbations Delta_A and Delta_v satisfying all three displayed conclusions. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, Theorem 4.5, eqs. (4.23)-(4.25)]

The parameter r is determined from the computed factors as their maximum off-diagonal block rank, after which c = b + 2r^(3/2) + p is formed. [PDF p. 12, printed p. 962, Section 4 opening; PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, Theorem 4.5]
hypotheses: The system printed in Theorem 4.5 is A_tilde x = v, and it is solved through L_tilde y = v followed by U_tilde x = y. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, Theorem 4.5]
L_tilde and U_tilde must be computed by Algorithm 1 (UFC) or Algorithm 2 (UCF); no other factorization variant is named in the theorem. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, Theorem 4.5]

The proof imports Theorems 4.2 and 4.3, whose hypotheses require un-tilded A to be nonsingular and the selected factorization algorithm to run to completion. These conditions are inherited rather than restated in Theorem 4.5. [PDF p. 19, printed p. 969, Theorem 4.2; PDF p. 21, printed p. 971, Theorem 4.3; PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, proof of Theorem 4.5]

Each triangular solve is performed blockwise in the order required by Theorem 4.4, using b by b diagonal solves and accumulated low-rank block products. [PDF p. 23, printed p. 973, Theorem 4.4; PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, eq. (4.22)]
All elementary arithmetic obeys the standard relative-error model with unit roundoff u. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 954, eq. (2.5)]
Each low-rank compression obeys Assumption 2.1, and the standing analysis assumes u is safely smaller than epsilon. [PDF p. 5, printed p. 955, Assumption 2.1]

The gamma indices used must be valid: in particular pu < 1 and 3cu < 1 are required by the definition gamma_k = ku/(1-ku). [PDF p. 4, printed p. 954, gamma definition; PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, eqs. (4.24)-(4.25)]
conclusions: There exist perturbations Delta_A and Delta_v such that (A + Delta_A)x_hat = v + Delta_v. The coefficient in this displayed conclusion is the un-tilded A. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, eq. (4.23)]
The matrix perturbation satisfies ||Delta_A|| <= (xi_p epsilon + gamma_p)||A|| + gamma_(3c)||L_tilde||||U_tilde|| + O(u epsilon). [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, eq. (4.24)]

The right-hand-side perturbation satisfies ||Delta_v|| <= gamma_p(||v|| + ||L_tilde||||U_tilde||||x_hat||) + O(u^2); gamma_p multiplies the entire parenthesized sum. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, eq. (4.25)]

With E_fac denoting the sign-adjusted perturbation in A + E_fac = L_tilde U_tilde, and E_L, E_U, e_v, and e_y denoting the two triangular-solve perturbations, the proof's exact compositions are Delta_A = E_fac + E_L U_tilde + L_tilde E_U + E_L E_U and Delta_v = e_v + L_tilde e_y + E_L e_y, before the final names and big-O bounds are adopted. [PDF p. 25, printed p. 975, proof of Theorem 4.5]
definitions_and_conventions: A_tilde is a BLR representation of dense A: diagonal blocks are retained as A_ii, while off-diagonal A_ij are replaced by low-rank A_tilde_ij. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 953, eq. (2.2)]
For i > j, A_tilde_ij = X_ij Y_ij^T; for i < j, A_tilde_ij = Y_ij X_ij^T; X_ij has orthonormal columns and both factors have dimensions b by k_ij. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 953, eq. (2.3)]
The rank k_ij is chosen minimally subject to ||A_ij - A_tilde_ij|| <= epsilon beta_ij and rank(A_tilde_ij) = k_ij. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 953, eq. (2.4)]
The base local convention is beta_ij = ||A_ij||, while the base global convention is beta_ij = ||A||. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 953, paragraph following eq. (2.4)]
Tildes mark BLR or low-rank represented quantities, while hats mark computed solve results in the theorem and proof. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, Theorem 4.5; PDF p. 25, printed p. 975, proof]

The final Delta_A and Delta_v are existential backward perturbations and are not the same intermediate perturbations initially denoted by those symbols in the proof; the proof uses primed final quantities before dropping the primes in the theorem statement. [PDF p. 25, printed p. 975, proof of Theorem 4.5]
implicit_context: Nonsingularity and factorization completion are inherited through Theorems 4.2 and 4.3 rather than explicitly quantified in Theorem 4.5. [PDF p. 19, printed p. 969, Theorem 4.2; PDF p. 21, printed p. 971, Theorem 4.3; PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, proof of Theorem 4.5]
The triangular-solve analysis is inherited from Theorem 4.4 separately for L_tilde and U_tilde. [PDF p. 23, printed p. 973, Theorem 4.4; PDF p. 25, printed p. 975, proof of Theorem 4.5]

For UFC, the finite xi_p bounds occur after the paper adopts scaled local/global thresholds; for UCF, the text states that such scaling is unnecessary. [PDF p. 17, printed p. 967, eqs. (4.13)-(4.15); PDF p. 22, printed p. 972, discussion after Theorem 4.3]

Theorem 4.4's solve constant is c_tri = b + r^(3/2) + p, whereas Theorem 4.5 uses the larger common constant c = b + 2r^(3/2) + p in its final bound. [PDF p. 23, printed p. 973, Theorem 4.4; PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, Theorem 4.5]

The theorem provides no independent bound on ||L_tilde||||U_tilde||, so growth or instability in the factorization remains visible in the backward-error estimate. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, eq. (4.24); PDF p. 19, printed p. 969, discussion above Section 4.1.3]
statement.algorithm_linkage: The permitted execution is either Algorithm 1, the left-looking UFC sequence update-factor-compress, or Algorithm 2, the UCF sequence update-compress-factor, followed by the block triangular solves L_tilde y = v and U_tilde x = y. Optional intermediate recompressions occur during LU updates and alter xi_p through Table 1. The proof uses Theorem 4.2 for UFC, Theorem 4.3 for UCF, and Theorem 4.4 for both solves. [PDF p. 13, printed p. 963, Algorithm 1; PDF p. 19, printed p. 969, Table 1 and Theorem 4.2; PDF p. 21, printed p. 971, Algorithm 2 and Theorem 4.3; PDF pp. 24-25, printed pp. 974-975, Theorem 4.5 and proof]
numerical_model: For each scalar operation, fl(x op y) = (x op y)(1 + delta), |delta| <= u, for addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 954, eq. (2.5)]

gamma_k = ku/(1-ku) is defined only when ku < 1; the paper explicitly allows positive non-integer indices, which covers indices involving r^(3/2) and c. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 954, gamma definition and following paragraph]
The compression model is A_tilde_ij = A_ij + Delta_A_ij with ||Delta_A_ij|| <= epsilon beta_ij, treating truncated-SVD rounding errors as negligible. [PDF p. 5, printed p. 955, Assumption 2.1]

The analysis is generic in unit roundoff u and does not fix Theorem 4.5 to IEEE single, double, or half precision. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 954, eq. (2.5); PDF p. 5, printed p. 955, Section 2.3 distinguishes experimental precisions from the analysis]
The standing regime is described qualitatively as u safely smaller than epsilon. [PDF p. 5, printed p. 955, paragraph after Assumption 2.1]
error_notions: The result is a joint normwise backward-error statement: both the coefficient matrix and right-hand side may be perturbed. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, eqs. (4.23)-(4.25)]

It is not a componentwise error guarantee; the paper explicitly explains that low-rank approximation errors generally hold only normwise. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 953, paragraph before the Frobenius-norm convention]

The coefficient perturbation combines low-rank truncation error, ordinary arithmetic error proportional to ||A||, and factor-growth-dependent arithmetic error proportional to ||L_tilde||||U_tilde||. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, eq. (4.24)]
The right-hand-side perturbation depends on both ||v|| and ||L_tilde||||U_tilde||||x_hat||. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, eq. (4.25)]
No forward-error or solution-relative-error bound is asserted in Theorem 4.5. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, complete statement of Theorem 4.5]
norms: Every unsubscripted norm in the analysis is the Frobenius norm. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 953, final paragraph]

The Frobenius norm is used normwise and is submultiplicative; the paper also uses the square-sum relation between block norms and the global Frobenius norm. [PDF pp. 3-4, printed pp. 953-954, Frobenius-norm discussion]

Accordingly, all matrix and vector norms displayed in (4.23)-(4.25) use the paper's unsubscripted norm convention. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 953, norm convention; PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, eqs. (4.23)-(4.25)]
constants_and_indexing: There are p block rows and columns, each block has order b, and n = pb. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 953, Section 2.1 after eq. (2.3)]

In the block triangular solve, x_i denotes x((i-1)b+1:ib), and a lower-triangular block row uses the sum over j = 1,...,i-1 before solving with the diagonal block. [PDF p. 23, printed p. 973, Theorem 4.4]
r is the maximum off-diagonal block rank of the computed LU factors, not the input BLR rank. [PDF p. 12, printed p. 962, opening of Section 4]
Theorem 4.4 uses c_tri = b + r^(3/2) + p; Theorem 4.5 defines c = b + 2r^(3/2) + p and uses gamma_(3c). [PDF p. 23, printed p. 973, Theorem 4.4; PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, eq. (4.24)]
xi_p equals 1 for local/no recompression, p for global/no recompression, p for local/with recompression, and p^2/sqrt(6) for global/with recompression. [PDF p. 19, printed p. 969, Table 1]
The right-hand-side bound uses gamma_p, with no p-1 offset, and the matrix factor term uses gamma_(3c), not 3 gamma_c. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, eqs. (4.24)-(4.25)]
higher_order_terms: The matrix perturbation retains an O(u epsilon) remainder. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, eq. (4.24)]
The right-hand-side perturbation retains an O(u^2) remainder. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, eq. (4.25)]

The exact pre-simplification matrix composition includes the second-order product Delta_L_tilde Delta_U_tilde, and the exact right-hand-side composition includes Delta_L_tilde Delta_y_hat. [PDF p. 25, printed p. 975, proof of Theorem 4.5]
The theorem does not state constants, signs, dimension dependence, or uniformity properties for either big-O remainder. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, eqs. (4.24)-(4.25)]
exceptional_values: The inherited factorization results are conditional on running to completion, so breakdown during block LU factorization is excluded. [PDF p. 19, printed p. 969, Theorem 4.2; PDF p. 21, printed p. 971, Theorem 4.3]
The inherited factorization input A is required to be nonsingular. [PDF p. 19, printed p. 969, Theorem 4.2; PDF p. 21, printed p. 971, Theorem 4.3]

The gamma expressions require their index times u to be less than one, including pu < 1 and 3cu < 1 for the final formulas. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 954, gamma definition; PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, eqs. (4.24)-(4.25)]

Overflow, gradual underflow, subnormal behavior, NaNs, and infinities are not separately addressed in the stated arithmetic model or Theorem 4.5. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 954, eq. (2.5); PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, Theorem 4.5]

No particular pivoting strategy is fixed by Theorem 4.5; the bound remains conditional and retains the computed factor norms. [PDF p. 13, printed p. 963, Algorithm 1 and Theorem 4.1; PDF p. 21, printed p. 971, Algorithm 2; PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, eq. (4.24)]

undebatable_constraints: The permitted BLR LU factors are those computed by Algorithm 1 or Algorithm 2. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, Theorem 4.5]
The computed solution must be obtained by the two triangular systems L_tilde y = v and U_tilde x = y. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, Theorem 4.5]

All three parts of the result must be preserved: the perturbed equation (4.23), the matrix perturbation bound (4.24), and the right-hand-side perturbation bound (4.25). [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, Theorem 4.5]
The matrix bound is ||Delta_A|| <= (xi_p epsilon + gamma_p)||A|| + gamma_(3c)||L_tilde||||U_tilde|| + O(u epsilon). [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, eq. (4.24)]
The right-hand-side bound is ||Delta_v|| <= gamma_p(||v|| + ||L_tilde||||U_tilde||||x_hat||) + O(u^2). [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, eq. (4.25)]
The final constant is c = b + 2r^(3/2) + p, with r the maximum off-diagonal rank of the computed LU factors. [PDF p. 12, printed p. 962, Section 4 opening; PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, Theorem 4.5]

The four xi_p values are exactly 1, p, p, and p^2/sqrt(6) for local/no recompression, global/no recompression, local/with recompression, and global/with recompression, respectively. [PDF p. 19, printed p. 969, Table 1]
The norm is Frobenius and the guarantee is normwise rather than componentwise. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 953, normwise-error and Frobenius-norm paragraphs]
The O(u epsilon) and O(u^2) terms may not be silently omitted. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, eqs. (4.24)-(4.25)]
The exact proof composition contains the solve-perturbation product terms before big-O simplification. [PDF p. 25, printed p. 975, proof of Theorem 4.5]

The factorization completion and nonsingularity conditions are inherited from the factorization theorems used in the proof. [PDF p. 19, printed p. 969, Theorem 4.2; PDF p. 21, printed p. 971, Theorem 4.3; PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, proof of Theorem 4.5]

ambiguities.issue: The theorem switches from A_tilde in its binder and system to un-tilded A in its conclusion and proof.
ambiguities.evidence: Theorem 4.5 begins with A_tilde and the system A_tilde x = v, but equations (4.23)-(4.24) and the proof use A. Section 2.1 separately defines A_tilde as a BLR representation of dense A. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 953, eqs. (2.2)-(2.4); PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, Theorem 4.5 and eqs. (4.23)-(4.24)]
ambiguities.impact: The paper strongly suggests that the backward perturbation is measured against the underlying dense A, but Theorem 4.5 does not explicitly restate the relation between its bound A_tilde and its concluding A; an extraction must preserve this notational switch rather than identify them silently. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, Theorem 4.5]

ambiguities.issue: The phrase local/global threshold in Table 1 hides an algorithm-dependent scaling convention.
ambiguities.evidence: Before the UFC summary, the paper adopts scaled local/global beta parameters in (4.13)-(4.15), whereas the discussion after Theorem 4.3 says UCF has no reason to scale the threshold. Table 1 labels its columns only local and global. [PDF p. 17, printed p. 967, eqs. (4.13)-(4.15); PDF p. 19, printed p. 969, Table 1; PDF p. 22, printed p. 972, discussion after Theorem 4.3]
ambiguities.impact: For UFC, applying the advertised xi_p coefficients to the unscaled beta_ij choices from (2.4) would omit diagonal-factor norm dependence; the precise threshold convention must therefore accompany the algorithm choice. [PDF pp. 16-17, printed pp. 966-967, eqs. (4.11)-(4.15)]

ambiguities.issue: The symbol c is used with different values in the triangular-solve theorem and final theorem.
ambiguities.evidence: Theorem 4.4 defines c = b + r^(3/2) + p, while Theorem 4.5 defines c = b + 2r^(3/2) + p and its proof subsequently writes the solve perturbation bounds using gamma_c. [PDF p. 23, printed p. 973, Theorem 4.4; PDF pp. 24-25, printed pp. 974-975, Theorem 4.5 and proof]
ambiguities.impact: The final result unambiguously uses the larger c and gamma_(3c), but the solve-stage constant should not be reported as though Theorem 4.4 itself stated that larger value. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, eq. (4.24)]

ambiguities.issue: The standing comparison u safely smaller than epsilon is qualitative.
ambiguities.evidence: The paragraph after Assumption 2.1 says u must be safely smaller than epsilon and assumes this throughout, without giving a numerical inequality. [PDF p. 5, printed p. 955, paragraph after Assumption 2.1]
ambiguities.impact: Apart from the explicit gamma-domain conditions, the precise admissible relationship between u and epsilon is not formally quantified. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 954, gamma definition; PDF p. 5, printed p. 955, Assumption 2.1 discussion]

ambiguities.issue: The constants hidden by O(u epsilon) and O(u^2) are unspecified.
ambiguities.evidence: Equations (4.24) and (4.25) display the two big-O terms without defining their constants or parameter dependence. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, eqs. (4.24)-(4.25)]
ambiguities.impact: The source supports only the asymptotic forms shown; it does not justify replacing them by zero or by explicit universal constants. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, eqs. (4.24)-(4.25)]

ambiguities.issue: No particular pivoting behavior is part of the theorem statement.
ambiguities.evidence: Algorithms 1 and 2 show block LU operations without a permutation or pivoting step, while the surrounding discussion treats pivoting separately; the formal results instead assume completion and retain ||L_tilde||||U_tilde||. [PDF p. 13, printed p. 963, Algorithm 1; PDF p. 21, printed p. 971, Algorithm 2; PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, eq. (4.24)]
ambiguities.impact: The theorem does not establish a pivot-growth bound or unconditional stability for a specific pivoting variant; numerical growth remains represented by the factor-norm product. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, eq. (4.24)]

contract_plain_english: Under the paper's standard floating-point model and truncated-SVD compression model, factor the printed BLR system A_tilde x = v using either UFC (Algorithm 1) or UCF (Algorithm 2), then perform the two ordered BLR triangular solves. [PDF pp. 4-5, printed pp. 954-955, eq. (2.5) and Assumption 2.1; PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, Theorem 4.5] Conditional on the inherited nonsingularity and runs-to-completion assumptions, the computed x_hat is the exact solution of a jointly perturbed system (A + Delta_A)x_hat = v + Delta_v, where the printed conclusion uses the underlying un-tilded A. [PDF p. 19, printed p. 969, Theorem 4.2; PDF p. 21, printed p. 971, Theorem 4.3; PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, eq. (4.23)] In Frobenius norm, ||Delta_A|| is bounded by (xi_p epsilon + gamma_p)||A|| + gamma_(3c)||L_tilde||||U_tilde|| + O(u epsilon), and ||Delta_v|| is bounded by gamma_p(||v|| + ||L_tilde||||U_tilde||||x_hat||) + O(u^2), with c = b + 2r^(3/2) + p and xi_p selected from all four entries of Table 1 according to threshold type and recompression use. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 953, norm convention; PDF p. 19, printed p. 969, Table 1; PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, eqs. (4.24)-(4.25)] The exact proof retains the products of the factor and triangular-solve perturbations before absorbing them into the displayed higher-order terms. [PDF p. 25, printed p. 975, proof of Theorem 4.5]
